answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost floor, not a vote count. Make every challenge answer escrow a bonded stake, forfeited when peer graders disagree, so a thousand cheap clones must lock a thousand real stakes. Random peer assignment with no kin splits an attacker across juries. Copying an answer replays as a duplicate on-ledger and burns the bond. A submitter crosses a graded prism: one identity, one stake, many reviewers, and the payout inlet slashes any jury-dissenter bond. Each grader keeps a juniper record of dissent votes, auditable at settlement.
